title: Incident bot collectors — phased rollout checklist
linked_artifacts: Confluence: Incident bot usage and escalation guidelines
Confluence: Runbook - triage with deploy + config context
body:
Purpose
- Provide a repeatable, low-risk rollout plan for incident-bot “context bundles” + collectors (deploy, config diff, saturation).
- Ensure fail-open behavior, minimal Slack noise, and compliance with redaction / restricted incidents.

Rollout owner(s)
- Delivery lead: Rafael Mendes (SRE)
- Incident workflow owner: Sean Gallagher
- Security reviewer: Marcus Lin
- Telemetry/metrics owner: Logan Wright / Allison Grant
- Platform/config stakeholder: Priya Natarajan / Ethan Park
- Program manager: Talia Benson

Definitions / configuration knobs
- Collectors:
  - Deploy collector: last N deploy events per service/region; link PR/pipeline.
  - Config diff collector: diff effective routing/policy snapshots (t-30m vs now) with redaction + allowlist.
  - Saturation collector: snapshot GPU/queue/throttle/contended scheduler + canonical dashboards.
- Posting modes:
  - Normal mode: bundle posted into incident thread.
  - Restricted mode: minimal summary in #incidents; full bundle in restricted channel (see allowlist).
- Feature flags / config keys (names may differ by environment; verify in config repo before proceeding):
  - incident_bot.enabled
  - incident_bot.collectors.deploy.enabled
  - incident_bot.collectors.config_diff.enabled
  - incident_bot.collectors.saturation.enabled
  - incident_bot.posting.channel_allowlist
  - incident_bot.posting.restricted_mode.enabled
  - incident_bot.posting.restricted_mode.channel
  - incident_bot.posting.rate_limit.max_posts_per_incident
  - incident_bot.posting.compact_formatting.enabled
  - incident_bot.collectors.timeout_ms (per collector)
  - incident_bot.collectors.cache_ttl_seconds
  - incident_bot.redaction.mode (strict)
  - incident_bot.redaction.allowlisted_keys

Success criteria (go/no-go)
- Within first 2–5 minutes of a SEV incident: responders get deploy + config + saturation evidence (where available) and links to canonical dashboards/runbooks.
- Bot does not slow incident workflow:
  - Bot bundle posting latency p95 <= 45s from trigger.
  - Collector timeouts respected; partial bundles render with clear “why missing” sections.
  - No sustained increase in metrics backend load (watch query rate + error budget).
- Noise: <= 1 “bot is noisy/unhelpful” report per week after Phase 2; formatting compact.
- Safety: no customer payloads/tokens posted; restricted-mode works reliably.

Pre-rollout checklist (must complete before any enablement)
1) Code + config readiness
- [ ] PRs merged for collector framework + formatting + fail-open behavior (ENG-2845).
- [ ] Feature flags wired and documented (ENG-2850 / incident-bot/pr_0133).
- [ ] Rate limiting enabled by default (incident-bot/pr_0127).
- [ ] Collector caching enabled with safe invalidation (incident-bot/pr_0129).
- [ ] Integration tests green in CI with recorded fixtures (ENG-2849 / incident-bot/pr_0130).
- [ ] Clear per-collector error sections (incident-bot/pr_0131).
- [ ] “Suspected change” heuristic (if enabled) is framed as heuristic; no definitive language (incident-bot/pr_0132). Default: OFF for initial phases.

2) Data sources validated
- [ ] Deploy events present in event stream for top 10 services (release pipeline emits standardized schema).
- [ ] Region tagging is consistent (no “us-east” vs “useast” drift; confirm normalization).
- [ ] Config snapshot endpoint meets latency SLO (region-aware); caching enabled; tested under load.
- [ ] Metrics backend endpoints for saturation queries are stable; dashboards exist + links correct.

3) Redaction + restricted-mode readiness (Security sign-off required)
- [ ] Redaction allowlist reviewed w/ Marcus Lin (no secrets, customer identifiers, tokens, request bodies).
- [ ] Config diff collector classifies fields as SAFE_TO_POST vs RESTRICTED; restricted fields never posted in normal mode.
- [ ] Restricted-mode channel created + membership policy defined.
- [ ] Audit logging enabled for bot outputs (at minimum: incident id, collector names, redaction decisions, post destination).
- [ ] “Fail closed on sensitive” behavior: when uncertain, omit + explain (“suppressed due to sensitivity”).

4) Observability of the bot (must exist before rollout)
- [ ] Bot health dashboard created (requests, failures, latency, per-collector timeout rate, Slack post failures).
- [ ] Alerts:
  - [ ] Bot posting failure rate > 10% over 10m (warning), > 25% over 10m (page SRE on-call only during beta).
  - [ ] Collector timeout rate > 20% over 15m.
  - [ ] Metrics backend 429/5xx spike correlated with bot query volume.
  - [ ] Slack API rate-limit errors > threshold.
- [ ] Log/trace links documented for debugging bot issues.

5) On-call enablement + documentation
- [ ] Confluence “Incident bot usage and escalation guidelines” updated.
- [ ] Runbook “triage with deploy + config context” linked in bot output.
- [ ] “How to request more context” command documented (if supported).
- [ ] Define feedback mechanism: emoji reaction + short form (“useful / noisy / wrong / missing”).

6) Rollback plan prepared
- [ ] Single switch to disable bot globally (incident_bot.enabled) tested in staging + prod.
- [ ] Per-collector disable switches tested.
- [ ] Channel allowlist can be emptied quickly (config rollout time known).
- [ ] If restricted-mode misroutes: disable restricted-mode posting immediately.

Phased rollout plan

Phase A — Staging + dogfood (SRE only)
Goal: confirm end-to-end wiring, formatting, and failure modes before adding more channels.
- [ ] Enable incident_bot.enabled in staging.
- [ ] Enable deploy collector only.
- [ ] Trigger synthetic incident and verify:
  - [ ] Post lands in thread within 45s.
  - [ ] Links resolve (PR, pipeline run, dashboard).
  - [ ] Region-aware deploy list matches expected service.
  - [ ] If deploy event missing, bot says “no recent deploy events found in last X min” (not blank).
- [ ] Enable config diff collector in staging.
  - [ ] Validate allowlisted keys appear; restricted keys suppressed.
  - [ ] Confirm diff time window (default t-30m) displayed clearly.
- [ ] Enable saturation collector in staging.
  - [ ] Validate queue depth and GPU metrics present; links correct.
  - [ ] Validate behavior when metrics delayed: collector returns “metrics delayed, last point at …” + dashboards.
- [ ] Run load test (bounded) to confirm caching prevents repeated heavy queries.

Phase B — Limited prod beta (2–3 rotations / allowlisted channels)
Recommended duration: 1 week.
- [ ] Select allowlisted channels:
  - [ ] #incidents (read-only: bot posts only within incident threads it is invited to / configured for)
  - [ ] #eng-oncall (optional: summary notifications OFF by default)
  - [ ] #incidents-restricted (restricted-mode full bundle)
- [ ] Configure incident_bot.posting.channel_allowlist to a small set.
- [ ] Set conservative rate limits:
  - [ ] max 1 bundle per incident per 10 minutes (tunable) OR “only on incident open + on demand.”
  - [ ] max_posts_per_incident set (e.g., 6).
- [ ] Enable “compact_formatting” by default.
- [ ] Enable deploy collector in prod beta.
- [ ] Enable config diff collector in prod beta.
- [ ] Keep saturation collector OFF for first 48 hours unless metrics backend load confirmed safe.
- [ ] Daily check-in during beta (15 min) with SRE + on-call:
  - [ ] Review “useful/noisy/wrong/missing” feedback.
  - [ ] Check bot health dashboard.
  - [ ] Review top 3 incidents for context quality.

Beta go/no-go gates (before expanding)
- [ ] No sensitive data leakage reports.
- [ ] Slack rate-limit errors under threshold.
- [ ] Bot posting latency p95 <= 45s; p99 <= 90s.
- [ ] At least 3 incidents where deploy/config context was used during triage (qualitative notes OK).
- [ ] Metrics backend impact acceptable (no new throttling).

Phase C — Expand to saturation collector + broader channel coverage
Recommended duration: 1–2 weeks.
- [ ] Enable saturation collector for allowlisted channels.
- [ ] Validate saturation signals align with standards:
  - [ ] queue depth
  - [ ] throttling / 429s
  - [ ] scheduler contention
  - [ ] GPU pressure / utilization (as defined by observability standards)
- [ ] Confirm guardrails to prevent high-cardinality query explosions are active.
- [ ] Expand allowlist to additional incident channels / regional incident rooms if used.
- [ ] Turn on “suspected change” heuristic only after confirming low false-positive rate; default remains OFF unless Sean + Rafael agree.

Phase D — GA (default-on in #incidents, restricted-mode enforced)
- [ ] Announce GA in #eng and #eng-oncall with “what changed / how to give feedback / how to disable in your thread.”
- [ ] Update onboarding docs for new responders.
- [ ] Ensure restricted-mode auto-detection rules are documented (what triggers restricted mode).
- [ ] Confirm monitoring and alert routing is correct (who gets paged for bot health issues).

Communication templates

1) Beta announcement (Slack: #eng-oncall)
Subject: Incident bot context bundles — limited beta (deploy + config)
Body:
- We’re enabling the incident bot collectors for a small set of channels this week.
- Expected: when an incident is declared, the bot posts a “Context bundle” with recent deploys + config diffs + links.
- Please react to the bot post with:
  - ✅ useful
  - 🟨 noisy
  - ❌ wrong/misleading
  - 🔎 missing key context
- Escalation: if you think sensitive data was posted, immediately notify #eng-security and set incident to restricted.

2) GA announcement (Slack: #eng)
- What’s new: context bundles on incident open + on-demand command.
- What’s included: deploys, config diffs, saturation snapshot, dashboards/runbooks.
- Safety: redaction + restricted-mode.
- How to opt out temporarily: disable flag for your service/channel (link to runbook).

Operational checklist during rollout week (daily)
- [ ] Review bot health dashboard (errors, latency, Slack failures).
- [ ] Sample 2 incident threads: check readability + accuracy.
- [ ] Check for redaction audit log anomalies.
- [ ] Confirm metrics backend query volume within expected range.
- [ ] Triage any “wrong/noisy” feedback and file issues with concrete examples + timestamps.

Rollback criteria (immediate disable if any true)
- Any confirmed sensitive customer data posted to non-restricted channel.
- Bot causes significant Slack spam (rate limiter not working) impacting incident comms.
- Metrics backend degradation attributable to bot (sustained 429/5xx and incident response affected).
- Widespread incorrect context (e.g., deploy collector maps wrong service/region) leading responders astray.

Rollback steps (order)
1) Set incident_bot.enabled = false (global) if safety/major disruption.
2) If limited blast radius: disable specific collector (e.g., incident_bot.collectors.config_diff.enabled = false).
3) Clear channel allowlist (stop posting) while leaving bot health checks running.
4) Announce rollback in #eng-oncall + #eng-sre with brief reason and next steps.
5) Open follow-up Linear issue(s) with incident/thread links + redaction audit evidence.

Open questions / follow-ups (track in Linear)
- Time window defaults (deploy: last 2 vs last 60m; config diff: t-30m vs t-60m) — confirm with on-call feedback.
- Canary/rollout metadata: highlight canary percent and phase (requires release metadata consistency).
- Restricted-mode triggers: define consistent signals (customer name present? incident label? pager rotation?) and document.

Sign-offs (required before Phase D GA)
- [ ] SRE (Sean Gallagher)
- [ ] Security (Marcus Lin)
- [ ] Observability (Logan Wright or Allison Grant)
- [ ] Platform/config (Priya Natarajan or Ethan Park)

Notes
- Keep language cautious: “possible overlap with degradation window” not “root cause.”
- Favor missing data transparency: if collector fails/omits, say why and where to look next.
- Prioritize readability in Slack: compact blocks, consistent timestamps (UTC + local optional), and clear links.
